units.citation: Akber et al. (2018). Storm protection service of the Sundarbans mangrove forest, Bangladesh. Natural Hazards.
units.quote:
Crop ﬁelds are usually lower than houses, and con-
sequently the water height was higher. It was lowest for site-A (1.66 m) and highest for
site-C (3.46 m). Flood water remained (WLF) about 5 days at site-A, and that was about
8 days at site-B and site-C.

relationship.outcome_raw: days that storm-surge flood water stayed in crop fields (waterlogging, WLF): mangrove-sheltered site-A vs unsheltered polder site-B

context.practice_as_described: No intervention: the EXISTING Sundarbans mangrove forest (natural reserve forest, Ramsar/World Heritage site). Site-A = Jiudhara union, Morrelganj, Bagerhat: 'a location in the shadow of mangrove and within a polder' (polder-35/2, embankment 4-5 m). BASELINE = site-B, Bara Bighai union, Patuakhali Sadar: 'a location not in the shadow of mangrove, but within a polder' (polder-43/2, same embankment height). Site-C (no mangrove, no polder) is a grey-infrastructure arm and is NOT the counterfactual used here. 'Polder' = an embanked low-lying area protected by an earthen dyke. 'Shadow of mangrove' = sheltered by the forest from the cyclone's seaward side (p5, Table 1).
context.note: Damage-cost-avoided household survey after super cyclone Sidr (15 Nov 2007; p1 'super cyclone Sidr', p3 'Category IV', 'wind speed up to 240 km/h and produced 6 m of tidal waves'). 300 household heads, 100 per site, 5 villages x 20 households per site; recall survey in Dec 2015, eight years after the event (p12: 'completely based on the memory of the respondents'). Kruskal-Wallis test across all THREE sites (Table 3, p8); no pairwise site-A vs site-B test, so significance left not_reported. Mangrove presence varies at site level only (one site per arm), so unreplicated=true. Confounds named by the authors: site-B about 5 km closer to the cyclone path (Table 1: 30 vs 25 km; p11), sites only 'anecdotally similar' in exposure; authors: 'this study is not enough to conclude with a value' (p12). Currency TK (1 US$ = TK 68 in 2007, Table 3 footnote). farming_system left blank: paddy with shrimp/aquaculture mixed culture, most respondents' primary occupation non-farm (Table 2). Mechanism stated by the authors: mangroves attenuate wind and storm surge (p3, p8, p10). Storm-surge flooding during the cyclone. Table 3 (p8): flooding in premises (FP) site-A 0.73 m, site-B 1.09 m, site-C 2.38 m; flooding in crop field (FCF) 1.66 / 1.98 / 3.46 m; waterlogging in field (WLF) 5 / 8 / 8 days (all H tests p<0.01 across three sites). Depths are respondent-recalled water heights, not measured flood depth (p8). One flood unit only (duration) to avoid counting the same surge three times; depths recorded here. Authors on p8: the difference 'might be caused by the presence of mangrove' (surge attenuation).

units.question: Akber 2018 says after cyclone Sidr flood water stayed in fields about 5 days behind the Sundarbans mangroves against 8 days at a similar site without them. We recorded less flooding, strong. This is existing forest, not planting, and the days are farmers' recall eight years later. The numbers match. Approve keeps it. Reject: oddly, protection from floods for tidal coastal planting rises from moderate to very high, and the flood rating from moderate to strong benefit. AI's view: Numbers and comparison match the quote; existing-forest status is already tagged.
